title: Economic Discourse
subtitle: Read the economy, comment on data, weigh the great debates

lessons.title: Le vocabulaire de la conjoncture
lessons.description: The precise language French commentators use to describe economic conditions, cycles and forecasts.

blocks.heading: La conjoncture: the temperature of the economy
blocks.body: French draws a sharp line between la conjoncture (short-term conditions, the current climate) and les facteurs structurels (deep, long-lasting features). A journalist who says «un problème conjoncturel» means it should pass; «un problème structurel» means it will not. This pair is the single most useful distinction in French economic commentary, and you will hear it in interviews, editorials and board meetings alike.

examples.french: La conjoncture s'est nettement dégradée depuis le printemps.
examples.english: Economic conditions have deteriorated markedly since the spring.

examples.french: Il s'agit d'un ralentissement conjoncturel, non d'un déclin structurel.
examples.english: This is a cyclical slowdown, not a structural decline.

examples.french: L'institut publie chaque trimestre une note de conjoncture.
examples.english: The institute publishes a quarterly economic outlook note.

examples.french: Le climat des affaires reste orienté à la baisse.
examples.english: The business climate remains on a downward trend.
examples.note: «orienté à la hausse / à la baisse» is standard commentary phrasing.

examples.french: Les difficultés du secteur sont structurelles et anciennes.
examples.english: The sector's difficulties are structural and long-standing.

blocks.tip: In French, «la conjoncture» alone is enough — you rarely need «économique» unless the context is ambiguous.

blocks.heading: The phases of the cycle
blocks.body: The cycle has a standard vocabulary in French: expansion, retournement, ralentissement, contraction or récession, then reprise and rebond. Note that «la récession» has a conventional technical meaning (two consecutive quarters of falling output) that commentators often invoke explicitly. «La reprise» is the return to growth; «le rebond» stresses the speed of it.

examples.french: Après trois trimestres d'expansion, on observe un retournement.
examples.english: After three quarters of expansion, a turning point is emerging.

examples.french: Deux trimestres consécutifs de recul: l'économie entre techniquement en récession.
examples.english: Two consecutive quarters of decline: the economy is technically entering recession.

examples.french: La reprise s'annonce lente et inégale selon les secteurs.
examples.english: The recovery looks set to be slow and uneven across sectors.

examples.french: Le rebond du troisième trimestre n'a pas effacé les pertes antérieures.
examples.english: The third-quarter rebound has not erased the earlier losses.

examples.french: L'activité s'essouffle sans pour autant se contracter.
examples.english: Activity is running out of steam without actually contracting.

blocks.tip: «Techniquement» before «en récession» signals the statistical definition rather than a judgment on lived conditions.

blocks.heading: Indicators and forecasts: hedging like a professional
blocks.body: French economic commentary is heavily hedged. Forecasts are «révisées à la hausse» or «à la baisse»; figures are «corrigés des variations saisonnières»; comparisons are made «en glissement annuel». Learning these fixed phrases lets you read a note de conjoncture without translating, and lets you write one that sounds native.

examples.french: L'institut a révisé sa prévision de croissance à la baisse.
examples.english: The institute has revised its growth forecast downwards.

examples.french: Les chiffres sont corrigés des variations saisonnières.
examples.english: The figures are seasonally adjusted.
examples.note: Often abbreviated CVS in French tables.

examples.french: En glissement annuel, les prix progressent de 2,4 %.
examples.english: Year on year, prices are rising by 2.4%.

examples.french: L'acquis de croissance atteint déjà 0,8 % à mi-année.
examples.english: The growth carry-over already stands at 0.8% at mid-year.

examples.french: Les indicateurs avancés laissent présager un redressement.
examples.english: Leading indicators point to a recovery.

examples.french: Sous réserve d'une stabilisation des prix de l'énergie, la prévision tient.
examples.english: Provided energy prices stabilise, the forecast holds.

blocks.tip: «Sous réserve de» and «toutes choses égales par ailleurs» are the two great disclaimers of French forecasting.

blocks.heading: Nominalisation: turning verbs into headlines
blocks.body: French economic prose prefers nouns where English prefers verbs. «Les prix ont augmenté» becomes «la hausse des prix»; «l'activité ralentit» becomes «le ralentissement de l'activité». This nominalisation compresses information and is essential for titles, summaries and note-taking. Build the noun, then attach the agent with «de» and the direction with «à la hausse / à la baisse».

examples.french: Le ralentissement de l'activité inquiète les industriels.
examples.english: The slowdown in activity is worrying manufacturers.

examples.french: La dégradation du climat des affaires se confirme.
examples.english: The deterioration in the business climate is confirmed.

examples.french: On note un redressement des carnets de commandes.
examples.english: A recovery in order books is noticeable.

examples.french: La révision à la baisse des prévisions a été mal accueillie.
examples.english: The downward revision of the forecasts was badly received.

examples.french: L'essoufflement de la reprise n'a rien de surprenant.
examples.english: The recovery running out of steam is hardly surprising.

blocks.tip: When you nominalise, keep the article: French says «la hausse des prix», never «hausse des prix» in running text.

blocks.heading: Hedging a forecast: conditional, «devrait» and «sous réserve de»
blocks.body: Forecasts in French are almost never stated in the plain future. Use the conditional («la croissance atteindrait 1,4 %») for unconfirmed figures, «devrait + infinitif» for expectations, and «sous réserve de» or «à condition que + subjonctif» for conditions. The conditional here is journalistic, not hypothetical: it signals that the number comes from someone else.

examples.french: La croissance atteindrait 1,4 % selon l'institut.
examples.english: Growth would reach 1.4% according to the institute.
examples.note: Conditional of attribution — the figure is not the writer's own claim.

examples.french: L'inflation devrait refluer au second semestre.
examples.english: Inflation should recede in the second half of the year.

examples.french: Sous réserve d'une détente des prix de l'énergie, la reprise se poursuivrait.
examples.english: Provided energy prices ease, the recovery would continue.

examples.french: À condition que la demande se maintienne, l'emploi progresserait encore.
examples.english: Provided demand holds up, employment would rise further.

examples.french: Toutes choses égales par ailleurs, l'effet resterait limité.
examples.english: All other things being equal, the effect would remain limited.

blocks.tip: Mixing the plain future with «selon» sounds naive in French: «selon l'institut, la croissance sera…» is better as «serait».

passages.title: Note de conjoncture — un printemps sans élan
passages.french:
Le ralentissement observé depuis janvier se confirme, sans pour autant tourner à la récession.
L'activité a progressé de 0,1 % au premier trimestre, après 0,3 % au trimestre précédent.
En glissement annuel, la croissance s'établit à 0,9 %, soit un point de moins qu'il y a deux ans.
Ce tassement tient d'abord à l'atonie de la demande intérieure, que rien ne semble relancer.
Le moral des ménages, mesuré par notre enquête mensuelle, recule pour le quatrième mois consécutif.
Les chefs d'entreprise interrogés décrivent un climat des affaires morose mais non alarmant.
Dans l'industrie, les carnets de commandes se dégarnissent ; dans les services, ils se maintiennent.
Il convient toutefois de distinguer ce qui relève de la conjoncture de ce qui relève du structurel.
Le déficit de compétitivité du tissu productif, lui, ne date pas de ce trimestre.
Nos indicateurs avancés laissent présager un léger redressement à partir de l'automne.
La croissance atteindrait alors 1,1 % sur l'ensemble de l'année, sous réserve d'une détente des prix de l'énergie.
Nous avons néanmoins révisé à la baisse notre prévision d'investissement des entreprises.
Une remontée trop rapide des taux constituerait le principal risque pesant sur ce scénario.
À l'inverse, un rebond de la consommation pourrait nous conduire à réviser nos chiffres à la hausse.
Toutes choses égales par ailleurs, l'économie devrait donc éviter la contraction.
Quoi qu'il en soit, aucun retournement franc n'est attendu avant le début de l'année prochaine.
passages.english:
The slowdown observed since January is confirmed, without however turning into a recession.
Activity grew by 0.1% in the first quarter, after 0.3% in the previous quarter.
Year on year, growth stands at 0.9%, that is one point less than two years ago.
This easing is due first of all to sluggish domestic demand, which nothing seems to be reviving.
Consumer confidence, measured by our monthly survey, is falling for the fourth month in a row.
The business leaders surveyed describe a gloomy but not alarming business climate.
In industry, order books are thinning out; in services, they are holding up.
It is nevertheless important to distinguish what is cyclical from what is structural.
The competitiveness gap in the productive base does not date from this quarter.
Our leading indicators point to a slight recovery from the autumn onwards.
Growth would then reach 1.1% for the year as a whole, provided energy prices ease.
We have nonetheless revised our forecast for business investment downwards.
Too rapid a rise in interest rates would constitute the main risk weighing on this scenario.
Conversely, a rebound in consumption could lead us to revise our figures upwards.
All other things being equal, the economy should therefore avoid contraction.
In any case, no clear turning point is expected before the beginning of next year.

lessons.title: Commenter des données
lessons.description: Describing charts, variations and proportions in French — including the number conventions that trip up English speakers.

blocks.heading: Naming the chart and its parts
blocks.body: Before commenting, you situate: «le graphique ci-dessus», «le tableau ci-contre», «la courbe rouge». French uses «l'axe des abscisses» for the horizontal axis and «l'axe des ordonnées» for the vertical one, and «la légende» for the key. A useful opener is «Ce graphique retrace l'évolution de… entre X et Y», which announces the variable and the period in one move.

examples.french: Ce graphique retrace l'évolution du chômage entre 2016 et 2024.
examples.english: This chart traces the evolution of unemployment between 2016 and 2024.

examples.french: En abscisse figurent les trimestres, en ordonnée les montants en milliards.
examples.english: The quarters are on the horizontal axis, the amounts in billions on the vertical axis.

examples.french: La courbe en pointillés correspond à la prévision.
examples.english: The dotted line corresponds to the forecast.

examples.french: D'après la légende, chaque couleur représente une région.
examples.english: According to the key, each colour represents a region.

examples.french: Le tableau ci-dessous détaille la répartition par tranche d'âge.
examples.english: The table below sets out the breakdown by age bracket.

blocks.tip: «Ci-dessus / ci-dessous / ci-contre» are standard in written commentary; in a presentation say «à l'écran» or «ici».

blocks.heading: Variation: de or à, points or percent
blocks.body: Two traps. First, «augmenter de 3 %» means a rise of three percent, while «augmenter à 3 %» means rising to reach the level of three percent — «de» is the amount of change, «à» is the destination. Second, a change from 5 % to 8 % is «une hausse de trois points», not «de trois pour cent»: percentages of percentages need «points de pourcentage».

examples.french: Le chiffre d'affaires a augmenté de 12 % en un an.
examples.english: Turnover rose by 12% in one year.

examples.french: Le taux de chômage est passé de 7,2 % à 6,8 %.
examples.english: The unemployment rate went from 7.2% to 6.8%.

examples.french: Cela représente une baisse de 0,4 point.
examples.english: That represents a fall of 0.4 percentage points.

examples.french: Les dépenses s'élèvent à 4,3 milliards d'euros.
examples.english: Spending amounts to 4.3 billion euros.
examples.note: «s'élever à» always takes the destination, never «de».

examples.french: La production a doublé, passant de 200 à 400 unités.
examples.english: Output doubled, going from 200 to 400 units.

examples.french: L'écart entre les deux régions s'est creusé de deux points.
examples.english: The gap between the two regions has widened by two points.

blocks.tip: «Passer de… à…» is the safest way to give a before-and-after without ambiguity.

blocks.heading: French number conventions
blocks.body: French writes the decimal separator as a comma and groups thousands with a thin space: 1 234,56. The percent sign is preceded by a space: 12 %. «Milliard» means a thousand million (English billion), and «un billion» in French means a million million — a classic false friend. Read 12,5 aloud as «douze virgule cinq».

examples.french: Le budget atteint 1 250 000 euros, soit 1,25 million.
examples.english: The budget reaches 1,250,000 euros, that is 1.25 million.

examples.french: La marge s'établit à 7,5 %, contre 6,9 % l'an dernier.
examples.english: The margin stands at 7.5%, compared with 6.9% last year.

examples.french: On parle de 3 milliards d'euros, et non de 3 billions.
examples.english: We are talking about 3 billion euros, not 3 trillion.
examples.note: «un billion» in French = a million million.

examples.french: Il faut lire douze virgule cinq, jamais douze point cinq.
examples.english: You must read twelve comma five, never twelve point five.

examples.french: Environ un tiers des ménages est concerné.
examples.english: Roughly one third of households is affected.

blocks.tip: In figures, French uses a non-breaking space before %, ! ? : ; — leaving it out looks like an English text in disguise.

blocks.heading: Agreement with quantities and fractions
blocks.body: «La plupart des ménages ont…» takes a plural verb, because the meaning governs. «Un tiers des salariés» allows both singular and plural, with a slight preference for the singular when the fraction itself is the point. After «plus d'un», French keeps the singular («plus d'un économiste le pense»), while «moins de deux» takes the plural. Percentages follow the noun that completes them.

examples.french: La plupart des ménages ont réduit leurs dépenses.
examples.english: Most households have cut their spending.

examples.french: Un tiers des salariés travaille à temps partiel.
examples.english: One third of employees work part-time.

examples.french: Plus d'un analyste s'est trompé sur ce point.
examples.english: More than one analyst got this point wrong.

examples.french: 30 % des entreprises interrogées prévoient d'embaucher.
examples.english: 30% of the firms surveyed plan to hire.

examples.french: Moins de deux ans ont suffi pour effacer la baisse.
examples.english: Less than two years were enough to erase the fall.

blocks.tip: With «une majorité de», the plural verb is now widely accepted: «une majorité de répondants estiment que…».

blocks.heading: Commenting verbs and their prepositions
blocks.body: Data commentary lives on a small set of verbs with fixed constructions: «augmenter de», «s'élever à», «passer de… à…», «représenter + quantité», «se traduire par», «témoigner de». Learn the preposition with the verb, not separately. Note also the impersonal openers «il ressort de ce graphique que…» and «force est de constater que…», both followed by the indicative.

examples.french: Il ressort de ce graphique que la tendance s'inverse.
examples.english: It emerges from this chart that the trend is reversing.

examples.french: Cette hausse se traduit par une perte de pouvoir d'achat.
examples.english: This rise translates into a loss of purchasing power.

examples.french: Le creux de 2019 témoigne d'un choc ponctuel.
examples.english: The 2019 trough is evidence of a one-off shock.

examples.french: Force est de constater que la prévision était trop optimiste.
examples.english: It has to be acknowledged that the forecast was too optimistic.

examples.french: Les chiffres bruts ne rendent pas compte des disparités régionales.
examples.english: The raw figures do not account for regional disparities.

blocks.tip: «Se traduire par» takes a noun; if you need a clause, switch to «signifie que + indicatif».

passages.title: Commentaire de graphique : ce que la moyenne ne dit pas
passages.french:
Le graphique ci-contre retrace l'évolution du revenu médian dans quatre régions fictives, de 2015 à 2024.
En abscisse figurent les années ; en ordonnée, les montants exprimés en milliers d'euros.
La courbe nationale, en trait plein, progresse régulièrement, passant de 21,4 à 24,8 milliers d'euros.
Cela représente une hausse de 15,9 % sur la période, soit environ 1,6 % par an.
À ce stade, le commentaire pourrait s'arrêter là et conclure à une amélioration générale.
Or les quatre courbes régionales racontent une histoire nettement moins uniforme.
La région Nord-Rivage plafonne depuis 2019 : son revenu médian n'a gagné que 0,3 point en cinq ans.
À l'inverse, la région Val-Central connaît un rebond marqué après le creux de 2020.
L'écart entre la région la mieux dotée et la moins bien dotée s'est creusé de 2,1 points de pourcentage.
Autrement dit, la moyenne progresse pendant que la dispersion s'aggrave.
Il convient donc de manier le chiffre national avec prudence.
Une moyenne qui monte n'exclut nullement qu'une partie de la population recule.
On notera par ailleurs que l'échelle des ordonnées ne part pas de zéro, ce qui accentue visuellement les pentes.
Ce choix graphique, fréquent, n'est pas malhonnête en soi, mais il exige d'être signalé.
Quoi qu'il en soit, aucune conclusion sur les causes ne peut être tirée de ce seul graphique.
Une corrélation apparente entre deux courbes ne vaut jamais démonstration d'une causalité.
passages.english:
The chart opposite traces the evolution of median income in four fictional regions, from 2015 to 2024.
The years are on the horizontal axis; on the vertical axis, amounts expressed in thousands of euros.
The national line, unbroken, rises steadily, going from 21.4 to 24.8 thousand euros.
That represents a rise of 15.9% over the period, that is roughly 1.6% per year.
At this stage, the commentary could stop there and conclude that there has been a general improvement.
And yet the four regional lines tell a distinctly less uniform story.
The Nord-Rivage region has plateaued since 2019: its median income has gained only 0.3 points in five years.
Conversely, the Val-Central region is experiencing a marked rebound after the 2020 trough.
The gap between the best-off and the worst-off region has widened by 2.1 percentage points.
In other words, the average is rising while the spread is worsening.
The national figure must therefore be handled with caution.
An average that rises in no way rules out part of the population falling behind.
It should also be noted that the vertical scale does not start at zero, which visually exaggerates the slopes.
This graphic choice, a common one, is not dishonest in itself, but it needs to be flagged.
In any case, no conclusion about causes can be drawn from this chart alone.
An apparent correlation between two lines never amounts to a demonstration of causality.

questions.prompt: What is the commentary's central point about the national curve?

It matches all four regional curves closely
It proves that regional policy has worked
questions.answer: It rises while regional dispersion worsens

questions.prompt: Why does the writer mention that the vertical scale does not start at zero?
options: Because it visually exaggerates the slopes and should be flagged
Because it is a dishonest manipulation of the data
Because it makes the regional gaps disappear
Because it means the figures are seasonally adjusted
questions.answer: Because it visually exaggerates the slopes and should be flagged

lessons.title: Les grands débats économiques
lessons.description: Presenting the major economic controversies in French with attribution, balance and precision.

blocks.heading: Attributing rather than asserting
blocks.body: In French economic writing, contested positions are attributed, not stated. The standard tools are «selon», «d'après», «pour les tenants de», «aux yeux de», «à en croire» (slightly sceptical), and the conditional of attribution. A sentence such as «les hausses de salaires alimentent l'inflation» asserts a disputed causal claim; «pour une partie des économistes, les hausses de salaires alimenteraient l'inflation» reports it.

examples.french: Pour les tenants de la relance, la dépense publique soutient l'activité.
examples.english: For supporters of stimulus, public spending sustains activity.

examples.french: Aux yeux de leurs détracteurs, ces mesures creusent le déficit sans effet durable.
examples.english: In the eyes of their critics, these measures widen the deficit with no lasting effect.

examples.french: À en croire certains commentateurs, la question serait tranchée.
examples.english: If certain commentators are to be believed, the matter is settled.
examples.note: «À en croire» often carries a hint of doubt.

examples.french: D'après ce courant de pensée, le marché s'autorégule à long terme.
examples.english: According to this school of thought, the market self-regulates in the long run.

examples.french: Ce point ne fait pas consensus parmi les économistes.
examples.english: This point is not the subject of consensus among economists.

blocks.tip: «Ne fait pas consensus» is the single most useful phrase for signalling a live controversy without taking sides.

blocks.heading: The classic fault lines
blocks.body: Four oppositions recur in French public debate: relance budgétaire versus rigueur; libre-échange versus protectionnisme; régulation versus dérégulation; and, more recently, croissance verte versus décroissance. Each camp has its own lexicon. Knowing which words belong to which side tells you where an editorial stands before it says so.

examples.french: Le clivage entre relance et rigueur structure le débat depuis des décennies.
examples.english: The divide between stimulus and austerity has shaped the debate for decades.

examples.french: Les partisans du libre-échange invoquent les gains de spécialisation.
examples.english: Free-trade supporters invoke the gains from specialisation.

examples.french: Leurs adversaires mettent en avant les délocalisations et les inégalités.
examples.english: Their opponents point to offshoring and inequality.

examples.french: Le courant décroissantiste conteste l'objectif même de la croissance.
examples.english: The degrowth current challenges the very goal of growth.

examples.french: Entre ces positions, un arbitrage politique reste nécessaire.
examples.english: Between these positions, a political trade-off remains necessary.

blocks.tip: «Un arbitrage» in economics means a trade-off, not an arbitration — a frequent false friend.

blocks.heading: Balancing a paragraph
blocks.body: A balanced C1 paragraph typically runs: statement of the debate, first position with its argument, «en revanche» or «à l'inverse» plus the second position, then a concessive close using «il n'en demeure pas moins que» or «reste que». Avoid ending on a verdict you cannot support; French readers expect «la question reste ouverte» rather than a forced conclusion.

examples.french: Il n'en demeure pas moins que les deux camps s'accordent sur le diagnostic.
examples.english: The fact remains that the two camps agree on the diagnosis.

examples.french: Reste que les données disponibles ne permettent pas de trancher.
examples.english: The fact remains that the available data do not allow the matter to be settled.

examples.french: À l'inverse, d'autres travaux nuancent fortement ce résultat.
examples.english: Conversely, other work strongly qualifies this result.

examples.french: Il serait imprudent d'en tirer une règle générale.
examples.english: It would be imprudent to draw a general rule from it.

examples.french: La question reste ouverte, faute d'un recul suffisant.
examples.english: The question remains open, for lack of sufficient hindsight.

blocks.tip: «Reste que» at the head of a sentence is elegant written French; in speech prefer «il n'empêche que».

blocks.heading: Concession: bien que, quoique, quand bien même
blocks.body: Balanced argument depends on concession. «Bien que» and «quoique» take the subjunctive; «même si» takes the indicative; «quand bien même» takes the conditional. Beginning a paragraph with a concession and closing it with «il n'en demeure pas moins que» is the classic French shape for weighing two positions fairly.

examples.french: Bien que la théorie soit élégante, elle résiste mal aux données.
examples.english: Although the theory is elegant, it stands up poorly to the data.

examples.french: Quoique contestée, cette mesure a été reconduite.
examples.english: Although contested, this measure has been renewed.

examples.french: Même si l'effet existe, il reste faible.
examples.english: Even if the effect exists, it remains small.

examples.french: Quand bien même la dépense augmenterait, l'impact serait limité.
examples.english: Even if spending were to increase, the impact would be limited.

examples.french: Il n'en demeure pas moins que le débat porte sur des valeurs.
examples.english: The fact remains that the debate is about values.

blocks.tip: «Quoique» in one word = although; «quoi que» in two = whatever. «Quoi qu'il en soit» means in any case.

blocks.heading: The subjunctive after verbs of doubt and judgment
blocks.body: Reporting disagreement calls for the subjunctive: «je doute que ce soit suffisant», «il est contestable que la mesure ait produit cet effet», «rien ne prouve que la baisse vienne de là». By contrast, verbs of assertion in the affirmative keep the indicative («il est établi que la production a reculé»), which is precisely how you mark a fact you are willing to endorse.

examples.french: Je doute que cette hausse soit durable.
examples.english: I doubt this rise is lasting.

examples.french: Rien ne prouve que la baisse vienne de cette réforme.
examples.english: Nothing proves that the fall comes from this reform.

examples.french: Il est contestable que le chômage ait diminué pour ces raisons.
examples.english: It is questionable that unemployment fell for these reasons.

examples.french: Il est établi que la production a reculé de 2 %.
examples.english: It is established that output fell by 2%.
examples.note: Indicative — a fact the writer endorses.

examples.french: On ne saurait affirmer que la causalité soit démontrée.
examples.english: One could not claim that causality has been demonstrated.

blocks.tip: «On ne saurait» + infinitif is a refined way of saying «on ne peut pas» in argumentative writing.

passages.title: Relance ou rigueur : anatomie d'un désaccord
passages.french:
Peu de querelles économiques ont la longévité de celle qui oppose relance budgétaire et rigueur.
Elle resurgit à chaque ralentissement, avec les mêmes arguments et un vocabulaire à peine renouvelé.
Pour les tenants de la relance, une dépense publique supplémentaire soutient la demande et évite que le creux ne se prolonge.
À leurs yeux, la dette contractée aujourd'hui serait remboursée par la croissance de demain.
À l'inverse, les partisans de la rigueur estiment que cet effet d'entraînement a été largement surestimé.
Selon eux, l'endettement finit par peser sur l'investissement privé et par contraindre les choix futurs.
Chacun invoque des travaux empiriques ; chacun conteste la méthode retenue par l'autre.
Un point mérite pourtant d'être souligné : les deux camps partagent une bonne part du diagnostic.
Nul ne nie que le tissu productif souffre, ni que les inégalités se soient creusées depuis dix ans.
Le désaccord porte moins sur les faits que sur la hiérarchie des risques et sur le rôle de l'État.

passages.english:
Few economic quarrels have the longevity of the one that pits fiscal stimulus against restraint.
It resurfaces at every slowdown, with the same arguments and a barely renewed vocabulary.
For supporters of stimulus, additional public spending sustains demand and prevents the trough from dragging on.
In their eyes, the debt contracted today would be repaid by tomorrow's growth.
Conversely, supporters of restraint believe that this knock-on effect has been largely overestimated.
In their view, indebtedness ends up weighing on private investment and constraining future choices.
Each side invokes empirical work; each contests the method chosen by the other.
One point nevertheless deserves to be stressed: the two camps share a good part of the diagnosis.
Nobody denies that the productive base is suffering, nor that inequality has widened over ten years.
The disagreement is less about the facts than about the ranking of risks and the role of the State.
This controversy cannot therefore be reduced to an opposition between austerity and generosity.
Although the models have grown more refined, they still rest on disputed assumptions.
Nothing proves, in particular, that the fiscal multiplier has the same value at the top and at the bottom of the cycle.
If certain commentators are to be believed, the matter has long been settled; the literature says the opposite.
The fact remains that a trade-off must be made, and that it is ultimately a political matter.
In any case, presenting either camp as irrational would be the most convenient of simplifications.
